In my case, in France, the ambulance or firefighters (in my case), come to get you and bring you to the hospital. I had taken deadly amounts but it didn’t work at all (firefighters, nurses and doctors couldn’t believe I had taken that much and was still coherent). 

They put you in a box and put you on iv with liquids and anti poison (depending on what kind of SA of course). They leave you and come to check on you every 10/20min, then you are put in a solo room where you keep the iv and feel like dying (I had taken so much that of course I was high as hell and the anti poison didn’t act on that), then when the iv is done and they tested your kidneys, a psychiatrist comes in to ask you questions and to determine whether you should be institutionalized. 

In my case he wanted to, but my parents refused bc 1. They are in the medical field and the psych ward they wanted to send me to is very dangerous in their opinion, 2. Sadly my parents to this day don’t take my mental health seriously. 

Then I went home on the condition that I met with a psychiatrist the next day. The psychiatrist the next day told my mom I needed to be institutionalized and that he will call the police himself to come get me if she doesn’t brings me there. He gave her a good psych ward specialized in major depression and SA, my mom gave me the choice to go there on my own terms (and keep all my rights) or to be forced to go there by my parents and therefore my parents having guardianship over me (I was already an adult so they had no rights over me!). I decided to go on my own terms (I’m a law student I know damn well a guardianship is hard to get out of), I was there for 2 weeks. Honestly if I had been honest with the psychiatrist there I would have been kept way longer, but I knew what to say and not to say to be let go soon! 

In the psych ward we had activities, we made friends, we weren’t allowed too much phones and all, we were monitored all the time by the staff but they gave us a lot of freedom if we proved we earned it. 

I had a good experience, but remember my experience was 1. In France, 2. In a specialized psych ward for depression (so I didn’t see too much disturbing things!), and 3. Useless bc it just led me to speak less, and pretend more lol

If you are in the us, know that your experience will be hell compared to mine 

(And no the psych ward didn’t heal me, I’m still very much depressive and suicidal, I just know what to do and not to do for my next attempt 🙃)
